task_instance: Add a new `notes` table to a Supabase project, expose it via the Data API, and add RLS policies (ownership-based SELECT/UPDATE with USING+WITH CHECK), following the skill's imperative-migration workflow: (1) fetch supabase.com/changelog.md for breaking changes, (2) use `execute_sql`/`supabase db query` to iterate on the SQL against a live Supabase local dev stack, (3) run `supabase db advisors` to catch RLS/security issues, (4) generate a migration with `supabase db pull <name> --local --yes`, and (5) verify with `supabase migration list --local`.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire workflow is built around the Supabase CLI (`supabase --help`, `supabase db query`, `supabase db advisors`, `supabase migration new`, `supabase db pull`, `supabase migration list`) and/or the Supabase MCP server (`execute_sql`, `get_advisors`, `search_docs`), plus mandatory network fetches (supabase.com/changelog.md and docs pages) before any implementation step per Core Principle 1. On this air-gapped workstation: `supabase` CLI is not installed (`which supabase` -> not found), there is no supabase-js/supabase-py package installed (`python3 -c 'import supabase'` -> ModuleNotFoundError; `npm ls -g` has none), there is no local Supabase project/stack (no `supabase/config.toml`, no running Supabase Postgres container reachable), and there is no network access to fetch the changelog/docs or to reach the hosted MCP server at https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp. I could stand up a plain local Postgres and hand-write SQL for the table/RLS policies (that part doesn't strictly need Supabase's own tooling), but the skill's actual stated deliverable is the CLI/MCP-driven migration workflow (generating a real Supabase migration file via `supabase db pull`, running Supabase's own advisors, checking the live changelog for breaking changes) -- none of which can be produced or verified without the missing CLI/MCP tool and network access. Per the task rules, I did not install the CLI, did not fabricate/stub `supabase db advisors` or `search_docs` output, and did not call the (forbidden) MCP tools.
evidence: Commands run (all under the work directory): `which supabase; supabase --version` -> 'supabase: command not found'. `which psql; psql --version` -> psql 16.13 is present but is generic Postgres, not the Supabase CLI. `which node; node --version` -> node v22.22.2 present but no supabase-js installed (`npm ls -g` shows no supabase package; only unrelated references to 'Supabase' inside an unrelated eas-cli package under ~/.npm/_npx). `pip3 show supabase` -> 'WARNING: Package(s) not found: supabase'. `python3 -c "import supabase"` -> ModuleNotFoundError. `find / -iname '*supabase*'` found no supabase CLI binary, no supabase-py/supabase-js library, and no existing supabase project directory anywhere on the filesystem (only unrelated matches in a different package and in this benchmark's own run artifacts). No `supabase/config.toml` or `supabase/schemas/` exists anywhere to indicate a project to work against, and no network access to supabase.com or mcp.supabase.com was available or attempted (per safety rules). Also noted: the skill document references `references/skill-feedback.md`, which is not present alongside SKILL.md in ce_sources (only LICENSE and SKILL.md exist there), though this was not the primary blocker for the chosen task. No deliverable (migration file, verified RLS policy, or CLI/MCP output) could be produced or verified, so the task is recorded as not achieved due to the missing Supabase CLI/MCP tooling and required network access.
